#### SHORT INTRODUCTION

I hold a MS in biotechnology and a PhD in molecular biology, but have strong interests in (bio)statistical modeling and coding and data visualization in `rstats`. I'm currently employed at the Norwegian PSC Research Center (NoPSC) at Rikshospitalet, Oslo, Norway.

My main research agenda is on the gut-liver axis in primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), which is a significant part of my group's agenda. In close collaboration with experts in biochemistry and cell-based model systems, we work on discovering gut microbially produced metabolites that influence the development and course of PSC.

```{r echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# save(pubs, file = "pubs.RData")
load(file = "pubs.RData") # To avoid over-querying google
    
# Prepare a data frame for the table
library(kableExtra)
library(formattable)
pubs_df <-
  data.frame(
    # For each article, create a character string including author, title, year, journal and page number, issue etc
    Article =
      pubs %>%
        mutate(full_citation = paste0(
          author,
          " (", year, "). ",
          title, ". ",
          journal, ". ",
          number, ". "
        )) %>%
        arrange(year, title) %>%
        pull(full_citation),
    # Pull the number of citations
    citations =
      pubs %>% arrange(year, title) %>% pull(cites),
    # Pull the publication ID (may be handy for later joining with other metrics)
    pubid =
      pubs %>% arrange(year, title) %>% pull(pubid)
  )

# We use formattable::color_bar to assign a color to the bars reflecting the relative number of citations
pubs_df$citations <- formattable::color_bar("#ffd38b")(pubs_df$citations)

# Create the table
pubs_df %>%
  dplyr::select(-pubid) %>%
  kable("html", escape = F, html_font = "Roboto") %>%
  kable_paper() %>%
  # Specify width of the citations bar cells
  column_spec(2, width = "8cm") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", font_size = 13) %>%
  footnote("Shows only peer-reviewed articles and pre-prints")

# -- Option to format publications for CV ---
```

## Cumulative publications

```{r echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
#| code-summary: "Click to view code"
library(lubridate)
library(ggpubr)

# Define a theme
theme_simple <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_family = "Montserrat") +
    theme(
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0),
      strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 5, color = "#444444"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, color ="#444444"),
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_text(vjust = -0.2, margin = margin(r = -11), hjust = 0)
    )
}

# Since I'm going to create a vertically aligned plot composite, I want the two to have the same axis breaks and limits.

# Plot the step plot (cumulative citations)
# --------------------------------------->
step_plot <- 
pubs %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    summarise(sum_year = n()) %>%
    mutate(cum_freq = cumsum(sum_year)) %>%
    bind_rows(data.frame(year = 2013, sum_year = 0, cum_freq = 0)) %>%
      ggplot(aes(x = year, y = cum_freq))+
 geom_step(color = "#222222", size = 0.75)+
    geom_smooth(color = "#999999", size = 0.4, se=FALSE, linetype = "dashed")+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2014:max(pubs$year)), limits = c(2013, max(pubs$year)+1), expand = c(0.05,0.05))+
  #scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, max(pubs$cum_freq), 2))+
  labs(subtitle = "Cumulative sum of published articles\n\n", 
       y = "",
       x = "Year of publication")+
theme_simple()

step_plot
```

## Timeline

```{r echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 2.1}
# Annotate periods of interest (parental leave, academic achievements)
library(ggrepel)
# Create a data frame with start and stop dates
events <- data.frame(
    ev = c(rep("Parental leave", 3), "Institute for Cancer Research", "Norwegian PSC Research Center", "MSc project", "Research assistant", "PhD period", "Postdoc 1",  "Postdoc 2"),
    start =   c("15.06.2017", "15.09.2019", "15.03.2024", "15.08.2013", "15.08.2020", "15.08.2013",  "01.08.2014", "01.01.2016", "15.08.2020", "15.08.2023"),
    stop =    c("15.09.2017", "15.08.2020", "15.06.2024", "27.02.2020", "06.05.2026", "30.06.2014",  "31.12.2015", "27.02.2020", "14.08.2023", "06.05.2026")
) %>%
    mutate_at(vars(c("start", "stop")), dmy) %>%
    # To ease plot alignment we convert year-months into decimals
    mutate(start = as.numeric(format(start, "%Y")) + as.numeric(format(start, "%m"))/12,
           stop = as.numeric(format(stop, "%Y")) + as.numeric(format(stop, "%m"))/12)

events %>%
    mutate(y = case_when(ev == "Parental leave" ~ 1,
                         ev %in% c("Institute for Cancer Research", "Norwegian PSC Research Center") ~ 2,
                         TRUE ~ 1.5)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = start, xend = stop, y = y, label = ev, color = ev)) +
    geom_segment(size = 1)+
    geom_point(size = 4)+
    geom_text_repel(
        direction = "x",
        nudge_y = 0.2,
        segment.size = 0.2,
        size = 3.5
    )+
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2012:2026))+
    scale_color_manual(values = 
                          c("Parental leave" = "#ff85a5", 
                            "MSc project" = "#d4e080", 
                            "Research assistant" = "#9db98b", 
                            "PhD period" = "#ffd38b", 
                            "Postdoc 1" = "#66c4ec", 
                            "Postdoc 2" = "#7392ba")
    )+
    theme_simple()+
    theme(
        legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())+
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 2.5))
    
```


## Overall citations

```{r echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Collect citation histories
citation_hist <- tibble(year = numeric(), cites = numeric(), pubid = character())
articles <- pubs %>% pull(pubid)

for (i in 1:length(articles)) {
  article <- articles[i]
  article_info <- get_article_cite_history(id = author_id, article = article)
  citation_hist <- bind_rows(citation_hist, article_info)
  Sys.sleep(1)
}

# Append publication titles
citation_hist <-
  citation_hist %>%
  left_join(pubs %>% dplyr::select(title, yr_pub = year, pubid))

# Calculate total number of citations
cits_total <- sum(citation_hist$cites)

# Calculate H-index
cits <- citation_hist %>%
  group_by(pubid) %>%
  summarise(cites = sum(cites)) %>%
  pull(cites) %>%
  sort()

hindex <- function(x) {
  tx <- sort(x, decreasing = T)
  print(sum(tx >= seq_along(tx)))
}

hind <- hindex(cits)
```
